Work in C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Next.js 16 + Prisma, an AI website builder called Kodely).

BUILD: two Builder/Editor features. Bundled because both touch `app/projects/[id]/Editor.tsx` and parallel edits to that file would collide.

## 1. Plan-before-spend — closing a claim the board wrongly marked shipped
A board card reads "✅ SHIPPED — MVP: transparent credit meter + pre-generation cost estimate". **Half of that is false.** `estimateCredits()` exists in `lib/credits.ts` and has **zero callers** — nothing shows anyone a cost before they spend. It was found when an SEO article claimed "you see an estimated cost range before you spend" and the claim could not be grounded.

Build the honest version:
- Before a build runs, show what it is likely to cost. `estimateCredits(kind)` returns `{low, high}` — 120–550 for a create, 60–300 for an edit.
- **Present it as a wide bracket, never a precise figure.** Read that function's own comment: measurements are 144 and 472 credits, a threefold spread across two samples, which it says plainly is not a distribution. Do not compute an average and present it as a prediction. If the estimate would exceed the user's remaining balance, say so *before* they press the button — that is the whole point.
- The user's own measured average (`averageBuildCredits`) is more honest than the global range once they have history. `components/CreditMeter.tsx` (READ ONLY) already does this and gates on a build count so it never presents a global constant as "your average" — follow the same rule.

## 2. User-facing SEO / meta panel
Generated sites get real `<title>`, meta description and OG tags — the builder is prompted to write them (`lib/agent.ts` SYSTEM, READ ONLY) and `lib/site-seo.ts` (READ ONLY) applies a backstop plus `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml`. **The user cannot see or edit any of it**, so a wrong title discovered after publishing means re-prompting the model and paying for a build.

Build a panel showing the current title / description / OG values for the project, and let the user edit them directly without a generation. Read `lib/site-seo.ts` carefully first to understand what is stored where and what the backstop does, and read `app/api/projects/[id]/publish/route.ts` to see when values are applied. **If saving these requires an API route outside your scope, do not create one — describe exactly what you need in your report.**

## Scope — YOU MAY ONLY CREATE/EDIT FILES UNDER `app/projects/[id]/`
Everything else is off limits. READ anything.

## Do not regress
`Editor.tsx` now carries: live progress narration, the building overlay, thumbs-up/down rating, zip download, the Enhance flow, low-credit warning, Stop/cancel, device-frame preview, a Cmd/Ctrl-K command palette, and connection-loss recovery. **All of it must keep working.** Read the file fully before editing.

Specific traps already hit in this file, do not repeat them:
- Two `aria-live` regions holding the same string made screen readers announce every progress line twice.
- The command palette became keyboard-dead when focus was outside the dialog — Escape needs a window-level net because the editor unbinds its globals while the palette is open.
- Copy must not claim engine behaviour that isn't true: on the live SDK engine an aborted build persists **nothing**, because `lib/agent-sdk.ts` returns before the diff loop.

## Constraints
- Preserve the accessibility bar: visible `focus-visible:` states, real labels, `aria-*` on stateful controls, no keyboard traps. Note a known pre-existing issue: the sidebar is `w-96` (384px) so there is horizontal overflow at 380px — do not make it worse, and do not attempt the responsive rework.
- **No new white text on the brand gradient** — fails contrast (worst 1.81:1), a known accepted issue.
- Match the existing idiom: `rounded-md`/`rounded-lg`, `text-xs`/`text-sm`, monochrome, `border-black/10 dark:border-white/10`.
- DO NOT modify: prisma/schema.prisma, anything under lib/, app/api/**, app/dashboard/**, app/settings/**, app/admin/**, app/globals.css, components/**, proxy.ts, deploy.sh, .env, package.json.
- No new npm dependencies. Do NOT run `npm run build`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `deploy.sh`.
- **HARD GATE: `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app lib components` must BOTH be clean — currently zero errors AND zero warnings.**
- A dev server may be on :3003. The Browser pane may not composite frames, so verify DOM and computed styles programmatically rather than by screenshot.

## Report back
Both features, exactly how you framed the cost estimate and what you refused to state, anything you needed outside your scope, what you verified in the running app, and confirmation that the existing editor features still work.

## 1. Plan-before-spend

`estimateCredits()` now has a caller. `page.tsx` resolves it server-side (`lib/credits.ts` touches Prisma at module scope, so it can never be imported into the client Editor) and passes `{create, edit}` plus a new `measuredBuilds` count down as props. The panel renders directly above Build/Apply, hidden while a build runs, and is wired to the Build button via `aria-describedby="kodely-cost-estimate"` — deliberately **not** a second `aria-live` region, so the progress line is still announced once.

**How I framed the number, and what I refused to say:**

- No history → the bracket only: `120–550 credits` (create) / `60–300` (edit), captioned *"A deliberately wide bracket from the handful of builds we have measured, not a prediction."* I did not compute 335, or "about 300", or any midpoint. Two samples 3x apart is not a distribution, and the function's own comment says so.
- With history → the bracket is replaced by `~{avg} credits`, captioned *"Averaged from your own builds (N charged so far). An average, not a quote."* The "your average" claim is gated on `measuredBuilds > 0` — the same `db.build.count({ status: "SUCCEEDED", creditsCharged: { gt: 0 } })` gate `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx` uses — so `averageBuildCredits()`'s silent 400-credit global fallback is never labelled as the user's own.
- Balance warning compares against the user's average when measured, and against the **top** of the bracket otherwise (warning on the 120 floor would never fire when it matters). It does not fire for a fresh 750-credit account against a 550 top — I checked that specifically, because `CreditMeter`'s comment records that `buildsLeft < 2` used to turn amber on day one.
- What I refused to state: any mid-build cutoff. I read `app/api/generate/route.ts` — the only pre-flight gate is `balance <= 0` (plus the spend cap), and `chargeForBuild` writes the real amount even when it takes the balance negative. So the copy says the truth: *"A build that costs more than you have still finishes and is charged in full; it's the next one that won't start."*

Not covered: the self-imposed **spend cap** is a second real pre-flight blocker (`getSpendCapStatus`) and the estimate ignores it. Worth a follow-up — the panel could warn when the estimate exceeds `cap.remaining` too.

## 2. SEO / meta panel

A fourth view (`SEO`) beside Preview/Code/History, plus a command-palette entry ("Search & social metadata", hint "no credits"). Not gated on `isFirstBuild`, because the head exists from the foundation onward.

There is **no SEO column anywhere** — the head of the project's own `index.html` is the storage. The panel reads the draft source `index.html` the Editor already holds, parses it with `DOMParser` (attribute order, quote style and entities are all things the builder writes freely and a regex would show back raw), and offers editable Title / Meta description / og:title / og:description with character counters against the ~60 and ~150 targets from `lib/agent.ts`'s SYSTEM prompt (guidance only — never blocks save).

A "What a visitor sees" column mirrors `applySeo()`'s fill rules exactly and badges each auto-filled value. I verified this by running the **real** `applySeo` from `lib/site-seo.ts` in Node against a foundation head and a realistic agent-written head and diffing against the panel's predictions — they match. That surfaced a genuine footgun the panel now makes visible: a blank `og:description` does **not** inherit your meta description; `applySeo` composes one generic string from the title and uses it for both.

**Pre-existing bug found (not fixed, out of scope):** `applySeo` reads `currentTitle` out of the raw HTML while it is still entity-encoded, then re-escapes it when composing the fallback description. A title of `Bloom & Co` yields a served `og:description` of `Bloom &amp; Co … — built with Kodely.`, so the literal entities show up in link previews. `lib/site-seo.ts` lines ~86-116.

## What I need outside my scope

Saving requires one route I did not create:

**`PUT /api/projects/[id]/seo`**
- Body: `{ title: string, description: string, ogTitle: string, ogDescription: string }`. Suggested caps: title 200, description 400 (generous vs. the 60/150 guidance).
- Auth: `requireUser()`, then scope by `{ id, userId }` in a single query (the `updateMany` pattern `app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts` PATCH already argues for).
- Must rewrite the head of `index.html` in **both** draft rows: `{published:false, kind:"source"}` (or the next build reverts the edit) **and** `{published:false, kind:"build"}` (or the preview and a subsequent publish still serve the old tags). Upsert `<title>`, `meta[name=description]`, `meta[property=og:title]`, `meta[property=og:description]`, HTML-escaping the values.
- Must **not** touch `{published:true}` rows — going live stays an explicit publish.
- Response: `{ ok: true }` is enough; the client calls the existing `refreshFiles()`, which re-reads source files and bumps the preview nonce.

Rather than ship a Save button that silently always fails, the panel probes `OPTIONS` on that path once on mount and says so concretely when it's absent (naming the missing route). I verified the probe's semantics against the running dev server: Next 16 answers **204** for an existing route handler with no `OPTIONS` export (`/api/projects/abc`) and **404** for a nonexistent one (`/api/projects/abc/seo`). Save is disabled with the amber note today; when the route ships, nothing in the client changes.

The dev server on :3003 has no authenticated session and I don't sign in on a user's behalf, so I could not click through the live editor. Instead:

I read `Editor.tsx` in full before editing. Untouched: live progress narration, BuildingOverlay, BuildRating, zip download, Enhance/Revert, low-credit header warning, Stop/cancel, device-frame preview, ⌘K palette, and connection-loss recovery. Specifically:
